How have we dealt with this situation and the risks that resulted from it at BaFin? What topics have we dealt with in 2024? And what priorities have we set? Answers to these questions can be found in this annual report. On the following pages it is clear: Our nearly 3,000 employees have committed themselves in various ways in the past year to a functional, non- gress and stable financial system that can be undertaken and trusted by people. nnamdnaS saihttaM/niFaB © Last year, we have been working intensively to make our prudential requirements for credit institutions more proportionate in order to relieve small institutions of bureaucratic burdens. In November, we published a supervisory communication, in which we pointed out the scope for shaping small credit institutions in their risk management. In addition, we introduced facilitations with this supervisory communication. About three quarters of German credit institutions are expected to benefit from this. In addition, in 2024, we have committed ourselves to reducing regulatory complexity and forwarding corresponding proposals to policy makers. We will also make concrete proposals to the new Federal Government on how we can reduce complexity in Germany and in Europe and achieve greater proportionality in financial market supervision and regulation. In BaFin itself, some things have changed in the past year. On 1 January, 2024, Julia Wiens, a mathematician and a stockholder, took over as Executive Director of the Supervision of Insurance and Pension Funds. In December, 2024, we announced that Raimund Röseler, Executive Director of the Supervision of Banks, will retire at the end of March 2025. Nikolas Speer succeeded him on 1 April 2025. Also, the current year 2025 holds some uncertainties for the financial sector. The geopolitical situation seems unstable, the economy is developing further swiftly.
